title: Depth equality for regular-sequence quotients of a regular local ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], let $c\ge0$, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in\mathfrak m$ be an $R$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. For $0\le i\le c$ put $R_i=R/(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$, with $R_0=R$. Each $R_i$ is a nonzero Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with maximal ideal the image of $\mathfrak m$, and satisfies $\operatorname{depth}(R_i)=\dim R_i$ [def-weil-pbc-depth, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. In particular this holds for $R/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$; the empty sequence is allowed.

source.place: Tags 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), last sentence, and 02JN (lemma-reformulate-CM), last assertion on every prefix quotient. The depth upper bound is Tag 00LK (lemma-bound-depth); extracted from returned item step 6.

proof.text: Put $I_i=(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$. Since every $f_j$ lies in $\mathfrak m$, $I_i\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Regular locality makes $R$ Noetherian. Apply the local-quotient statement to $I_i$: $R_i$ is nonzero and local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/I_i$. Apply Noetherian permanence to the surjection $R\to R_i$. Thus these structure assertions hold for every $0\le i\le c$, independently of the depth calculation.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), proof on quotients; Tags 00E9 (lemma-characterize-local-ring) and 07BJ (lemma-characterize-local-ring-map), local quotient structure.

proof.text: We prove by induction on $i\le c$ that $\operatorname{depth}(R_i)\ge\dim R_i$. For $i=0$, write $d=\dim R$. By the definition of regular local ring choose $d$ generators $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ of $\mathfrak m$. The regular-generator theorem makes this an $R$-regular sequence. Consequently the definition of depth gives $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge d$. Here $\mathfrak m R=\mathfrak m\ne R$, so the supremum branch of that definition applies. This also covers $d=0$ using the empty regular sequence.

source.place: Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), regularity of minimal maximal-ideal generators and its last sentence; Tag 00LI (definition-depth).

proof.text: For the induction step let $i<c$ and $S=R_i$. Step 1 supplies its nonzero Noetherian local structure. The image $x$ of $f_{i+1}$ belongs to $\mathfrak m/I_i$ and is a nonzerodivisor on $S$ by the given regular-sequence condition. Apply the one-nonzerodivisor Cohen--Macaulay quotient theorem with $e=\dim S$ and the inductive bound $\operatorname{depth}(S)\ge e$. It gives $\dim(S/xS)=e-1$ and a regular sequence of length $e-1$ in its maximal ideal, hence depth at least that dimension. Identify $S/xS$ with $R_{i+1}$ explicitly: send the double class of $r$ to its class modulo $I_i+(f_{i+1})=I_{i+1}$. Its inverse sends the latter class to the double class; the ideal equality proves both maps well-defined and their composites fix every representative. They carry the image of $\mathfrak m$ to the image of $\mathfrak m$. Prime ideals correspond under these inverse maps, preserving strict inclusions, so dimensions agree. Likewise regular sequences correspond: the induced maps on each successive quotient conjugate the multiplication maps and preserve nonzeroness. Thus their sets of regular-sequence lengths in the maximal ideals agree, and their depths agree by definition. This proves the inductive bound for $R_{i+1}$ without assuming that $S$ remains regular local.

source.place: Tag 02JN (lemma-reformulate-CM), last assertion, iterating its one-element case; Tag 00LF (definition-regular-sequence), the next element on a prefix quotient.

proof.text: For each $i$, apply the depth upper bound to the nonzero finite $R_i$-module $M=R_i$, generated by $1$. Its support contains every prime $\mathfrak p$: if $1/1=0$ in $(R_i)_{\mathfrak p}$, some $s\notin\mathfrak p$ satisfies $s\cdot1=0$, forcing $s=0\in\mathfrak p$, a contradiction. Thus the support is the whole prime spectrum, whose chain dimension is $\dim R_i$. The bound gives $\operatorname{depth}(R_i)\le\dim R_i$. Combine this with the inductive lower bound to obtain equality for every prefix. Taking $i=c$ proves the final-quotient assertion. For $c=0$ the same argument consists of the base case and this upper bound.

lean.statement: theorem regular_sequence_quotients_depth_eq (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] (rs : List R) (hmem : ∀ x ∈ rs, x ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (hregular : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R rs) : ∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ rs.length → Nontrivial (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (rs.take i)) ∧ IsNoetherianRing (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (rs.take i)) ∧ ∃ hQ : IsLocalRing (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (rs.take i)), @IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (rs.take i)) _ hQ = (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.ofList (rs.take i))) ∧ (@IsLocalRing.depth (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (rs.take i)) _ hQ (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (rs.take i)) _ _ _ : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (rs.take i))
